thread.title: Spotify Stock Surges To Record High On Second-Quarter Subscriber Gain

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Spotify Stock Surges To Record High On Second-Quarter Subscriber Gain
text:
Streaming music leader Spotify Technology ( SPOT ) added more paying subscribers than expected in the second quarter, giving its shares a boost on Thursday.
X Spotify added 8 million paying subscribers in the second quarter, double the number it added in the first quarter. It ended the June quarter with 83 million paying subscribers worldwide, up 40% year over year. Analysts polled by Reuters expected 82 million subscribers.
However, average revenue per user (ARPU) declined 12% year over year to the equivalent of $5.83 in the second quarter. The Stockholm-based company reports financial results in euros.
"Growth in Family and Student plans continues to weigh on ARPU, as does the shift in market mix as we grow faster in relatively lower ARPU geographies like Latin America, Southeast Asia, and other newly launched markets," the company said in a news release . "Changes in foreign exchange rates also contributed to the year-over-year decline in ARPU. Excluding the impact of foreign exchange rates, ARPU would have been down 6% year over year."

It reported 101 million monthly active users of the ad-supported music tier, down 1 million from the first quarter. But the number rose 23% year over year from the 83 million users it reported for the same quarter last year.
Spotify stock fell as much as 4% in premarket trading on the stock market today , but it soon rebounded. It ended the regular trading session up 4.4% to 196.28. In intraday trading, it hit a record high of 198.99. Spotify went public on April 3, starting at 165.90.
Spotify's revenue rose 26% year over year to $1.52 billion in the June quarter. The company's premium subscriptions accounted for 90% of revenue, with advertising making up the rest.
The Swedish company lost the equivalent of $2.62 a share in the second quarter. That compares with a loss of $1.36 a share in the year-earlier period.
The company expects to add 3.5 million paying subscribers in the third quarter, based on the midpoint of its guidance. That would bring its total paying subscribers to 86.5 million. It forecasts ending the year with 93 million to 97 million premium subscribers.
Spotify competes in music streaming with Apple ( AAPL ), Amazon.com ( AMZN ), Alphabet ( GOOGL ), Pandora Media ( P ) and others.
Spotify Stock Gets Price-Target Hikes RBC Capital Markets analyst Mark Mahaney found the second-quarter report encouraging. He reiterated his outperform rating on Spotify stock and raised his price target to 215 from 210.
"Music is going streaming. Streaming is going global. Spotify is the global leader (40% of all paid subscribers) and we believe it has sustainable advantages," he said in a report.
Spotify's report delivered solid results and guidance, Evercore ISI analyst Anthony DiClemente said in a report.
"While the longer-term debate around streaming music economics is far from settled, we would count Q2 as a clear win for SPOT," he said. "Results should enhance investors' confidence in the company's ability to execute in the near term."
DiClemente maintained his outperform rating on Spotify stock and upped his price target to 210 from 200.
